consolidated_diary:
The strongest lesson from this game is that this player pool rewards narrow, adjudication-testable agreements far more than broad alignment talk. Exact one-turn border compartments worked repeatedly. As Germany, I built durable safety by getting literal no-touch deals from England, France, Austria, and Italy: specific spaces named, specific turn only, adjudicated immediately. Those deals held over and over. The mistake was not in using that method; the mistake was stopping at safety and finishing on only 8 centers. Future rule: use exact compartments to lock borders, then spend that safety on growth before a third party runs away.

A second major lesson: distinguish between “non-interference reliability” and “positive tactical support reliability.” Several powers were very good at the first and much worse at the second. England is the clearest case. As qwen/qwen3.5-27b playing England, he was extremely reliable about not touching agreed zones. From 1901 through 1910, exact promises like “no move/support/convoy touching HOL, KIE, DEN, HEL, BEL” held again and again. He also honored early macro understandings like Denmark for Germany, Norway for England. But when he promised positive tactical help for Belgium, that was much shakier. In Spring 1902 he did deliver F ENG S A HOL-BEL exactly, which won Belgium. But in Spring and Fall 1903 he talked about supporting BEL and then did not, because his own anti-France operations took priority or his wording left an escape hatch. Conclusion: qwen3.5 is probably still the most trustworthy model in the pool, consistent with the previous game where it was a very loyal France, but trust it most for clean border discipline and clear reciprocal structure, not for speculative tactical lending unless the exact order is simple and aligned with its main theater.

qwen/qwen3.6-plus as France was also highly board-honest. France repeatedly renewed a literal Burgundy compartment and later a BEL/BUR compartment: no PAR/MAR support touching BUR, no move/support touching BEL, etc. France openly contested Belgium early and said so plainly in advance; this was competitive, not deceptive. Over many years France never turned the quiet border into a surprise stab as long as the exact compartment was preserved. The useful read is that qwen3.6-plus will tell you when interests diverge, but can still be a very stable technical neighbor if the border terms are explicit and limited. As with qwen3.5, that kind of quiet border should be converted into growth elsewhere rather than passively enjoyed forever.

anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 as Italy was the biggest positive surprise. Italy repeatedly honored exact one-turn no-touch terms around TYR, BOH, and MUN for years. More importantly, when it finally sent an exact anti-Turkey package in Spring 1910, it executed essentially exactly as proposed, and our coordinated A PRU-WAR with A SIL support succeeded. That is valuable evidence that Claude can be an excellent coalition partner when the plan is concrete, local, and adjudication-testable. This partly fits the prior-game lesson from Claude-as-Russia: tactically truthful in narrow windows, but strategically dangerous if allowed to snowball. Same pattern here. Italy was tactically reliable with me, but by 1910 it had reached 13 centers. So future rule with Claude: do precise one-turn business and use it for real gains, but do not let repeated tactical honesty lull you into tolerating long-term overgrowth.

x-ai/grok-4.1-fast as Russia was the least trustworthy actor on literal wording. In Fall 1901, after agreeing to no move touching LVN, Russia ordered MOS-LVN. In Spring 1902, after another restricted-zone deal, it used A LVN-STP, again exploiting wording around “touching LVN.” Later it abandoned ambiguity and became openly hostile, repeatedly signaling and executing pressure on SWE, PRU, SIL, BER, and DEN. The useful read is twofold: first, Grok will sometimes use clever wording dodges rather than direct lies, so agreements must specify both destination and origin if relevant; second, once hostile, it is fairly straightforward and predictable. Against Grok, do not grant strategic concessions on the basis of partial compliance. If allied, require extremely literal terms and verify them one turn at a time. If opposed, expect direct, announced pressure rather than subtle diplomacy.

google/gemma-4-31b-it as Turkey fit the broader prior read that gemma is dangerous and not to be trusted strategically, but this game refined the picture. Early on Turkey mostly sent vague “stability” language and refused precise eastern non-touch terms. Once strong enough, it attacked hard and concretely: by Fall 1910 it launched a full-scale WAR attack with MOS-WAR and LVN/UKR support. However, when exact one-turn DMZs were finally reached in 1908 and Spring 1909, Turkey did honor them literally: it stayed off PRU/SIL/BER/MUN/BOH when promised. That means gemma can keep a tight local term for a turn if it sees immediate utility, but you should still assume strategic hostility and opportunism. Never extrapolate a one-turn Turkish DMZ into broader safety. Also note that a single unsupported poke at gemma is unlikely to work if it is alert: my Fall 1909 A PRU-WAR failed because Turkey anticipated it with GAL-WAR supported by LVN.

deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro as Austria was notably more reliable than gemma had been as Austria in the previous game. Deepseek repeatedly honored exact one-turn compartments on BOH and TYR and kept the German border quiet for years. This is consistent with the older read of deepseek as tactically honest on narrow local commitments. The right way to use deepseek is to compartmentalize clearly and keep bargains narrow. It may still pursue its own growth hard elsewhere, but on a demilitarized border it is usable.

My own tactical lesson is embarrassingly simple: stop issuing sloppy support orders. Across several years I created avoidable trust damage with malformed or mis-aimed supports like HEL supporting an English move into NTH despite a no-touch agreement, or void supports that made me look careless. In this pool, technical sloppiness matters because the strongest relationships are built on literal compliance. Before finalizing orders, sanity-check every support for legality and for whether it “touches” a promised zone even if tactically void.

Strategically, Germany showed both the power and the limitation of the compartment style. Exact western and southern quiet let me secure Belgium, Holland, Sweden, and the core with remarkable safety. But I spent too many years merely containing Russia and then Turkey instead of cashing in. The right adjustment for future games is not to abandon the board-proof method; it is to use it more aggressively. Once two borders are quiet, force the third front with concrete coalition plans. The Spring 1910 strike with Italy worked because it was exact, local, and synchronized. That is the template: real growth comes from precise multi-unit operations, not from endless mutual reassurances.

Actionable summary for future games: trust qwen3.5 the most on exact non-interference; qwen3.6-plus is also board-honest and stable if terms are explicit; Claude is excellent for exact tactical coalitions but must be contained before it grows too large; Grok requires the strictest wording and still should be treated as low-trust; gemma can honor a one-turn local term but remains strategically dangerous; deepseek is good for compartmentalized local peace. Above all, write exact one-turn deals, verify by adjudication, and then turn quiet borders into expansion before the board balance gets away from you.
final_goals: Fulfill the exact England compartment literally: no German move, support, or convoy touching NTH, ENG, NWY, LON, EDI, or LVP, and stay entirely out of BRE; expect England to keep HOL, KIE, DEN, HEL, and BEL untouched.

Fulfill the exact France compartment literally: no German move or support touching BUR or PIC, stay entirely out of BRE, give no German support touching BRE, and give no anti-France help from BEL; expect France to keep BEL and BUR untouched.
Fulfill the exact Italy compartment literally: no German move or support touching BOH or TYR, and no German support against TRI or VEN; expect Italy to keep TYR, BOH, and MUN untouched.
Recover SWE immediately with F BOT-SWE supported by F BAL.
Keep WAR, BER, BEL, KIE, DEN, and the core safe with legal low-risk orders; avoid malformed or impossible supports.
Maintain pressure on Turkey without accepting vague stability language; no Turkey agreement was accepted for F1910M.
Use the quiet west and south to prepare a broader 1911 anti-Turkey coalition if exact compartments continue holding.
Track Italy carefully: tactically reliable on exact orders, but now growing very fast and could become the next major strategic problem after Turkey weakens.
